newsitem.title: UK: Summary of latest opinion polls on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Summary of latest opinion polls on EMU.

text.p: The following is a summary of findings from recent independent opinion polls and surveys about European economic and monetary union (EMU).

GERMANY, July 18 - More than half of Germans fear the single European currency would negatively affect their savings and the economy and around two thirds thought the euro would be weaker than the mark, a survey conducted by the Institute for Market, Opinion and Economic Research showed.
SWEDEN, July 11 - One in three Swedes now support EMU participation, compared to one in four a year ago, a Gallup poll for business daily Dagens Industri showed.
GERMANY, July 2 - Four in 10 Germans firms expect EMU to be delayed, a survey by business magazine "Impulse" showed. Two percent said monetary union would never happen.

BRITAIN, July 2 - Almost half of British exporters oppose a single currency while 44 showed approval of EMU, a poll by international credit insurer NCM and the UK Institute of Export showed. The greatest dissent was from small firms.
GERMANY, June 29 - Sixty percent of Germans do not believe EMU will start on time, a survey for news magazine Der Spiegel showed.

DENMARK, June 22 - Danish resistance to economic and monetary union and other European projects has firmed since the Amsterdam summit, while most voters are undecided on the accord itself, a Gallup survey in the daily Berlingske Tidende said. It showed 50 percent opposed Danish EMU membership and 42 percent were in favour, compared with 49 percent against and 41 percent for monetary union in a March 1997 poll.

DENMARK, June 20 - The first Danish opinion poll conducted since EU leaders agreed to reform the EU treaty showed a small majority would vote to ratify it if a referendum were held now. The survey by the Greens polling unit, published in the business daily Borsen, showed 28.7 percent would vote to accept the new treaty and 22.0 percent would reject it, with the rest unsure how they would vote.
SWEDEN, June 18 - The number of Swedish market players that expect EMU to start on time was 81 percent in June, pollster Temo said. This compares with 82 percent in May.

EUROPE, June 17 - A telephone survey of around 6,000 people in seven EU countries published in Brussels by French bank Sofinco showed that 43 percent thought the introduction of the euro would be more inconvenient than beneficial. Thirty-two percent were in favour, while 25 percent either didn't know or couldn't say.

GERMANY, June 14 - A slim majority of Germans is against the planned single European currency with the strongest opposition coming from eastern Germany and left-leaning voters, a survey by the Forsa institute found. The survey found that 51 percent opposed the euro's introduction while 34 percent were in favour.

EUROPE, June 13 - Expectations that Italy will join core European countries in founding EMU in 1999 edged up in a week in which France turned the spotlight on job creation and growth, prices monitored by JP Morgan showed. Though the perceived likelihood of Spain and Portugal joining their ranks drifted down, hopes of the U.K. and Ireland joining EMU from the outset took the biggest battering, according to the JP Morgan "EMU calculator", derived mainly from the interest-rate swaps market. The probability of Irish membership tumbled to 41 percent from 54 percent last week and 63 percent in mid-May, while the implied likelihood of the U.K. joining slumped to 38 percent from 45 percent a week ago and a post-election high of 53 percent at the end of May.

GERMANY, June 12 - Almost half the German population is fearful of Europe's planned single currency because of worries the euro will be worth less than their German mark, an opinion survey conducted by the Wickert Institute said. The poll said 47 percent of 870 adults surveyed were frightened by the proposed single currency while 53 percent were not concerned.

GERMANY, June 12 - Europe's single currency may be unpopular in Germany but it will not become a campaign issue next year because the pro and anti camps are not clearly defined along party lines, according to leading pollster Elisabeth Noelle-Neumann. Head of the Allensbach Institute and doyenne of German opinion researchers, she said her surveys showed 52 percent of Germans were against the euro and this would not change much before the September 1998 election.

GERMANY, June 12 - Fifty-four percent of Germans surveyed in the Allensbach Institute's latest monthly poll said they expected EMU to start on time even though 52 percent said they were against it. Only 22 percent said they supported the single currency.

FRANCE, June 11 - A majority of French people think the new Socialist-led government should continue talks with its European partners to find new conditions for joining a single currency rather than doing everything possible to hit the Maastricht treaty criteria, according to a CSA poll. Fifty-eight percent of 1,000 French people polled on June 9 said they believed France should continue talks, rather than impose new austerity to hit the strict three percent deficit target, even if this risked compromising the move to a single European currency. Twenty-seven percent of those polled said France should do everything possible to hit the deficit target.

DENMARK, June 9 - Danish resistance to EMU has changed little over the past three months, an opinion poll published in the financial daily Borsen said.The survey, by Greens polling institute, showed 55.9 percent of respondents saying that Denmark should stick to its existing policy of staying out of monetary union, compared to 55.6 percent in a March poll. The survey showed 32.5 percent in favour of EMU compared with 33.4 percent in March, while the number of don't knows grew to 11.6 percent from 10.9 percent. -- London Polling Unit tel: +44 171 542 5223
